data.description:
## Problem statement

Work items that have passed through planning (stage `plan_complete`) are
sometimes left with `assignee: "Map"` (the producer identity) instead of being
cleared to empty. The plan skill's terminal transition calls
`StatusLifecycle.update_status(item_id, "open", stage="plan_complete")`
expecting the assignee to be released, but `should_release_assignee()` returns
`False` for Map because Map is classified as a producer hold. Items that
originally had Map assigned by intake (or by the herdr downtime dispatcher)
therefore retain the Map assignee after planning completes.

Evidence: MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E and MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS in tce-main-street are
both at `plan_complete` with `assignee: "Map"`.

## Users

- **herdr downtime dispatcher** — auto-dispatches items for processing; items
  stranded with Map cannot be re-dispatched because a non-empty assignee is a
  scheduling hold.
- **Map (producer)** — the producer has decided that `Map` is **not** a
  persistent hold marker: a lingering `Map` assignee after a skill run is
  indistinguishable from a deliberate producer park and strands the item.
- **Agents running any skill** — need one consistent rule: every terminal
  transition releases the assignee, so no skill can leave a scheduling hold
  behind on success or failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every skill terminal transition — **success or failure** — clears the
   persisted `assignee` to empty, including when the assignee is `Map`.
2. The rule applies to **all skills** (intake, plan, implement, audit,
   find-related, effort-and-risk, refactor, and any future skill), not only the
   plan skill.
3. The release is enforced in the shared terminal-transition choke point
   (`StatusLifecycle.update_status` and the context-manager exit paths) so a
   skill cannot reintroduce the hold by omission or by using a direct durable
   write.
4. `needsProducerReview` remains the **only** persistent-hold signal: releasing
   the assignee must never clear the `needsProducerReview` flag, and a
   `needsProducerReview` item must still be observable as awaiting producer
   review after its assignee is released.
5. Regression tests cover, table-driven across skills, both success and
   failure terminal paths and assert that a pre-existing `Map` assignee is
   released while the `needsProducerReview` flag survives.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (assignee-release invariant), `README`, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular any text that currently
   describes `Map` as a persistent producer hold.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Items that finish any skill run — successful or failed — are always released
for dispatch, so planned and implemented work no longer gets stranded behind a
lingering `Map` assignee.

## Constraints

- `Map` is no longer a persistent-hold marker; the producer's deliberate hold
  is represented by `needsProducerReview` alone (producer decision, this
  intake).
- The change must be in shared infrastructure (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
  and `skill/shared/claim_release.py`), not per-skill patches.
- The existing backstops (session-end `release_session_claim`, `signal_release`,
  `reap_stale_claims`) must stay consistent with the same predicate.
- Scope-creep risk: broader claim-lifecycle rework (e.g. dispatcher identity
  handling) is out of scope and should be recorded as linked work items.

## Existing state

- `StatusLifecycle.update_status()` with `release_assignee=None` calls
  `should_release_assignee()`, which returns `False` for Map, so Map is never
  cleared by the automatic release mechanism.
- The plan skill SKILL.md documents: "the terminal transitions below release any
  claim the item already carried", but the implementation does not release Map.
- The plan skill claims with no assignee itself — the Map is inherited from
  intake or from the herdr downtime dispatcher.
- `should_release_assignee()` is shared by all release paths (lifecycle, session
  backstop, reaper), so it is the single predicate to change.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` currently describe `Map`
  as a sanctioned persistent hold — that documentation is now wrong and must be
  updated.

## Desired change

Remove the producer-assignee exemption from the release predicate so that every
terminal transition (success or failure) releases any assignee, including
`Map`, in the shared choke point. Keep `needsProducerReview` as the sole
persistent-hold signal, and update the invariant documentation and regression
matrix accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee()`,
  `is_producer_assignee()`, `_release_skip_reason()`, `release_claim()`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status()`,
  `_auto_release_requested()`, `_should_release_assignee()`, `_restore_original()`
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — assignee-release invariant wording (Map no longer a hold)
- `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` — invariant reference documentation
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — plan status-lifecycle section
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — implement status-lifecycle section
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — intake assignee-release note
- `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — regression matrix (success +
  failure, Map pre-claim)

## Related work

- SA-0MW0F91KN004J06U: Remove assignee when a session finishes (completed)
- SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH: Enforce assignee release on every terminal outcome across all skills (completed)
- SA-0MW0X5W01008IY7Z: Close coverage gap: Release covers any non-producer claim (completed)
- SA-0MVVF7CZ6002UDKU: Document the assignee-release invariant (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK: T1: Table-driven assignee-release regression matrix (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL: Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ: Migrate callers and pin intentional holds (completed)
- SA-0MVVF75ZA007XNKB: Release assignee on signal, timeout and drive paths (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the assignee-release invariant apply to `Map` when a work item
  transitions to `plan_complete` (i.e. should `Map` be released at planning
  completion), or should `Map` always be preserved as a persistent producer
  hold regardless of stage?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "yes release the assignee, *always*
  whether a skill succeeds or fails."
- Q: "If `Map` should be released at `plan_complete`, should the fix adjust
  `should_release_assignee()` (shared predicate) or have the plan skill
  explicitly clear the assignee in its terminal transition?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "in terminal transitions, whether
  success or failure."
- Q: "Does this apply only to the plan skill, or to all skills (implement,
  intake, audit) that inherit a `Map` assignee?"
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): "all skills."

Research: inspected `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` and
`skill/shared/claim_release.py`; confirmed `should_release_assignee()` returns
`False` for `Map` (`is_producer_assignee`) and that all release paths share
that predicate. Inspected the two cited items in
`../tce-main-street` (`MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`, `MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS`) and
confirmed both sit at `plan_complete` with `assignee: "Map"`.

Documented assumption: since `Map` is no longer a hold marker, the
`needsProducerReview` flag is the sole persistent-hold signal. Releasing the
assignee on a `needsProducerReview` handoff therefore does not lose the
producer's intent — the flag still holds the item for producer review. The
`needsProducerReview` flag must never be cleared by the release.
data.title: Planned items are still left with an assignee
